claims.claim: The song is X-Kid by Green Day, presented on bass, and it came with a cassette.
claims.assessment: Article states a video showing the song playing on a cassette tape was released to the band channel on 19 December 2012. Title makes no claim that this upload contains that video.

claims.claim: X-Kid came with a cassette tape video.
claims.assessment: Stated in "Background and release". The cassette video is a separate release from this performance.

claims.claim: The cassette video was posted to Green Day's own channel on 19 December 2012.
claims.assessment: Same sentence, with the date and the official channel named.

claims.claim: X-Kid was cut at Jingletown Studios in Oakland.
claims.assessment: Infobox records the recording location as Jingletown Studios, Oakland, California.

claims.claim: Recording ran between February and June 2012.
claims.assessment: Infobox gives 14 February to 26 June 2012. Copy rounds to the month.

claims.claim: Rob Cavallo produced alongside the band.
claims.assessment: Infobox lists Rob Cavallo and Green Day as producers.

Player duration in the description screenshot shows 4:05. The single is listed at 3:42 on the song page and 3:41 in the album track list, so no exact runtime for the studio version is asserted in the copy.

claims.claim: The note highway stays up the whole way and a section can be taken at the viewer's own speed.
claims.assessment: Describes the Rocksmith chart overlay visible in the video still and the standard playback controls. Not a claim about the game build or difficulty.

claims.claim: Live requests open on Kick, a Twitch mirror runs at the same time, and Discord is the community link.
claims.assessment: Standing channel practice restated in house style: Kick first, Twitch second, Discord last, one URL each. Stream timing is not asserted.

claims.claim: Quiz: X-Kid was recorded at which Oakland studio? Options Jingletown, Ocean Way and Studio 880.
claims.assessment: Answer A, Jingletown, per the infobox. Ocean Way and Studio 880 are real rooms used only as options; the copy asserts no fact about them. The answer is not in the description.

claims.claim: Dedicated play-along, routed to the Rocksmith 2014 Bass Play Along playlist rather than the genre or All Genres lists.
claims.source: User standing rule, recorded in Ver 3.0/TXT/Play_Along_Series_ID_Map.md
claims.assessment: Matches the rule applied to every earlier play-along. The user status line for 0008 reads "Genre Added"; that report is recorded in the evidence section and not reinterpreted.

distinct_fact_and_source: The cassette tape video with its 19 December 2012 date, plus the Jingletown recording window and producers. Different from 0027, which uses the Billboard chart run and the A.V. Club Kerplunk comparison, and from the three Shorts, which use the Entertainment Weekly pick, the album title pun on Tre Cool and the early album release. Sources: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/X-Kid ; https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/%C2%A1Tr%C3%A9!
uniqueness_assessment: Five-word n-grams checked against every _03 - Copy.md in the repository and against the delivered copy in the Abigail, A-M-E-R-I-C-A, Masterpiece, MCR and Green Day playlist files. Zero shared five-word phrases with the corpus and zero between the five X-Kid packages. Format statements and CTA shapes are deliberately worded apart from the A-M-E-R-I-C-A and Abigail play-along packages. The gate report also returns zero cross-video signals.
uncertainties_and_removed_claims: The studio version runtime is given as 3:42 on the song page and 3:41 in the album track list, so no runtime for the studio recording is stated. The earlier claim that the song deals with the loss of a friend was carried by 0008 before this pass; it is not reused here because the copy now leans on the cassette video and the studio facts, and the article only says it deals with the suicide of a close friend, which is heavier than the previous wording implied. The earlier "bittersweet" framing is dropped. Stream timing, playlist membership and current pin state are not asserted. Historical screenshots cannot establish live settings.
